standalone_production_findings.trigger: Construct on real SQLite, call stop(), then add 500 distinct events without calling flush().
standalone_production_findings.actual: 500 audit rows persisted. add unconditionally flushes when queued length reaches batch size; stop only prevents periodic timer creation.
standalone_production_findings.test_change: Rename the existing one-event/fake-timer case to the periodic-timer behavior it actually exercises; do not claim writes are prohibited after stop.

standalone_production_findings.trigger: queueMax=2; enqueue oldest, pause its actual insert before delegation, start flush, enqueue middle and newest so overflow drops oldest from queue, release insert, flush again.
standalone_production_findings.actual: Real SQLite contains oldest and newest, while middle is absent and pending is empty. The completing flush splices batch.length from the trimmed queue, deleting an entry it did not write.
standalone_production_findings.test_change: Existing bounded-queue test now verifies oldest eviction with distinct durable identities when no write is in flight; the separate concurrent production flaw is not claimed fixed or regression-protected.

inspection_limitations: Simulation uses real CellReserveBook/ReservePlacer/mintEpoch/seat ordering within separate modeled director, socket, poll, ledger/reconcile and dead-man orchestration. All 29 runtime cases and ten explicit fault rows passed; model fault toggles validate observers, not production SQL/session mutations or production throughput.

Blackbox runs real Node children, loopback HTTP/JWKS/WebSocket and SQLite on this Linux host. Test-only controlled clock advances server time for confirmation/cooldown; bounded polling waits for actual persisted state or asynchronous evacuation completion. No macOS/Windows runtime was exercised; process launches now use the existing cross-platform spawnProcess wrapper.

Main blackbox scenarios deliberately share an evolving relay process, including restart and later drain; this batch preserves their ordering. Subprocess close barriers protect cleanup, but this is not proof of distributed crash recovery across remote hosts.

PostgreSQL validation uses the existing shared local server and an exclusively owned database. Fixed test schemas are serialized within the postgres project. Server configuration, preloads, roles and other databases were not changed. This is local SQL/catalog/lock evidence, not hosted Cloud SQL network/failover evidence.
Historical baseline schemas intentionally remain independent old snapshots. Root compatibility suite passes; their files are not refreshed to match current production.

schema-lock-target fail-closed policy covers its explicit MUST_PARSE forms. Unsupported ALTER RESET/default forms can return undefined; the retained live-schema census only proves all currently emitted relay DDL is supported, not universal DDL safety.

StatementRecordingDatabase observes the delegated transaction API outcome; COMMIT is now success-only and a thrown operation is labeled ROLLBACK. It is not a native SQL wire trace and does not prove exact round trips when BEGIN/acquisition fails before the callback. The standalone probe verifies actual callback-entered rollback and committed DDL.

reserve-mode-cell.nextFrame has no early close/error rejection; current consumers remain bounded by harness deadlines. It was retained unchanged because the selected source has no declarations and existing callers exercise real served behavior.

Unused exported transitionInvite/control-continuity/splice predicate and EvacuationCommitSchema models were not deleted from production. Their test-only duplicate state machines and constant inventories were removed or consolidated into real execution evidence.

Initial development runs caught a same-cell seeded-control expected upsert count, a wrong live-state label, an accidentally removed error import, expensive deep comparison of an 8 MiB Buffer, and RelayDatabase EXPLAIN result normalization. Final runs listed above passed after test-only corrections. The standalone probe also needed row-value normalization for SQLite null-prototype result objects; final probe passes.
